maintainer: razzfazz.ai GmbH — Member of SEQIS Group

tiers.core: Always-on foundation; runs unconditionally, cannot be disabled.

networks.default: Bridge network all services share; addressed by container name via Docker DNS.
networks.ssrf_proxy_network: Internal-only network for SSRF-isolated outbound HTTP (Dify code/HTTP nodes via Caddy:8195).

legend.edge: Caddy (ports 80/443) is the sole external entry point; every user-facing UI is gated by Authentik SSO forward-auth.

core.name: Core Infrastructure
core.purpose:
The always-on foundation every other module builds on. Caddy is the sole
external entry point — it terminates TLS, reverse-proxies every subdomain,
and enforces Authentik SSO via forward-auth (plus an internal SSRF proxy on
:8195). Authentik provides identity, SSO, OIDC and group-based access
control. PostgreSQL (pgvector) is the shared relational + vector database
with a separate tenant DB per service. Valkey is the shared cache / task
queue. A Postfix relay sends mail; the backup service snapshots all Docker
volumes on a cron schedule (encrypted). docker-socket-proxy brokers a
locked-down Docker API to the few services that need it; autoheal restarts
any container that goes unhealthy. The Setup, Config, Help, Licenses and
Backup web UIs round out the operator surface.
user_facing_capabilities: Single sign-on across every app with one identity (Authentik).
Self-service config portal to enable/disable modules, manage secrets, run backups, view governance checksums.
Guided first-time setup wizard and an offline documentation hub.
Automated encrypted nightly backups of all data volumes, with a restore UI.
Per-app access control via Authentik groups.
use_cases: Admin enables a new module from the Config portal and it appears, SSO-gated, within minutes.
Operator rotates a secret or takes a governance checksum snapshot before an audit.
Recover a service from a nightly backup after a bad change.

talks_to.purpose: Caddy reverse-proxy + forward-auth for every gated subdomain
shared DB for Authentik + every tenant

chat.name: Chat (Open WebUI)
chat.purpose:
A full-featured, ChatGPT-like workspace for talking to the box's local LLMs.
Multi-model conversations, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) over uploaded
documents, web search grounding via SearXNG, voice in/out via the speech
services, a custom "pipelines" extension layer, and multi-user access control
through Authentik SSO. It is the primary day-to-day interface most users see.
user_facing_capabilities: Chat with local models (qwen3.6 by default) — fully private, nothing leaves the box.
Upload documents (PDF, DOCX, etc.) and ask questions over them (RAG with reranking).
Ground answers in live web results via SearXNG web search.
Dictate by voice and have responses read back (STT/TTS).
Switch models per conversation; manage prompts, knowledge collections, and per-user chat history.
Extend behaviour with pipelines (filters, custom tools, observability hooks).
use_cases: Team AI assistant for drafting, summarising, translating, brainstorming.
Private document Q&A over contracts, manuals, or internal wikis.
Code review and generation against pasted snippets.
Research with web-grounded, citation-style answers.

talks_to.purpose: LLM call tracing via the global pipeline filter (when observability enabled)

dify.name: Workflows (Dify)
dify.purpose:
A visual, low-code platform for building LLM applications — AI agents, RAG
pipelines, chatbots, and multi-step workflow automations — without writing
code. Drag-and-drop a workflow, wire in the box's local models, document
knowledge bases, HTTP calls (through the SSRF-safe proxy), and code nodes
that run in an isolated sandbox. Publish flows as chat apps or as APIs.
user_facing_capabilities: Build AI workflows visually (LLM, knowledge-retrieval, condition, code, HTTP, tool nodes).
Create RAG knowledge bases from uploaded documents and query them in flows.
Run sandboxed Python/Node code nodes safely inside a workflow.
Publish a workflow as a hosted chat app or call it as a REST API.
Call internal doc tools (docling/tika/presidio) and web search from a flow.
use_cases: Customer-support / triage bots over a curated knowledge base.
Document pipelines: PDF → extract → classify → structured JSON (e.g. the PSA CMT demo).
Multi-step autonomous agents that chain tools and models.
API-driven LLM features embedded into other internal apps.

talks_to.purpose: SSRF-protected outbound HTTP for HTTP/code nodes
web search + document tooling from flows

llm-legacy.name: LLM Inference — GPUStack 0.7.1 + AMD Vulkan (stable default for AMD)
llm-legacy.purpose:
The model-serving engine that downloads, loads, and serves LLMs over an
OpenAI-compatible API to the whole stack. This is the STABLE production
default for AMD Strix Halo boxes: GPUStack 0.7.1 with a locally-built
Vulkan runner, validated leak-free under stop/start cycles. A model-sync
sidecar mirrors the active model list into Open WebUI; an Ollama-compatible
proxy lets legacy Ollama tools talk to it.
user_facing_capabilities: Serve local chat / coding / vision / embedding / reranker models over one OpenAI-compatible endpoint.
Manage models (download, start/stop, scale replicas) from the GPUStack dashboard.
Offload models to the AMD GPU (VRAM) for fast inference, fully on-box.
Expose an Ollama-compatible API for tools that expect Ollama.
use_cases: Back the Chat, Dify, RAG, and agent modules with private inference.
Run qwen3.6 at 1M context for chat/coding/vision on a single Strix Halo box.

talks_to.purpose: serves chat, dify, cognee, lightrag, agents, openhands via :9090

llm-cpu.name: LLM Inference — GPUStack 0.7.1 CPU (stable default for CPU)
llm-cpu.purpose:
The stable CPU-only inference path (llama.cpp under GPUStack 0.7.1) for
boxes without a supported GPU. Same role and surfaces as llm-legacy —
OpenAI-compatible serving, model-sync, Ollama proxy — without GPU offload.
user_facing_capabilities: Serve local LLMs + embeddings on CPU-only hardware over an OpenAI-compatible API.
Manage models from the GPUStack dashboard.
use_cases: Run the stack on a CPU-only VM or appliance (e.g. demo / test boxes).
Route heavy inference to a remote GPU worker while the CPU box stays the control plane.

llm.name: LLM Inference — GPUStack 2.1.x (experimental)
llm.purpose:
Upstream GPUStack v2.1.x with custom backends (kyuz0 ROCm runner for AMD
Strix Halo, ggml-org llama.cpp:server for CPU, built-in vLLM for NVIDIA).
Opt-in path for the newest features while the v0.7.1 lines remain the
stable defaults. NVIDIA installs use this unconditionally.
user_facing_capabilities: Serve local models with the latest GPUStack feature set and per-model runner containers.
Hardware overlay (amd/nvidia/cpu) selects the right inference backend automatically.
use_cases: NVIDIA boxes (vLLM backend).
Early adoption of new GPUStack capabilities on AMD/CPU.

monitor.name: Monitoring (Komodo)
monitor.purpose:
A web dashboard to monitor and manage every Docker container in the stack —
real-time logs, resource usage, restart/stop controls, and deployment
history. Runs its own database (FerretDB over a dedicated Postgres) so it
never contends with the main DB.
user_facing_capabilities: View live logs and resource usage for any container.
Restart / stop / start individual services from the browser.
Track deployment and update history.
use_cases: On-call triage: inspect a failing container's logs and bounce it.
Capacity review across the running stack.

talks_to.purpose: Mongo-compatible document store on a dedicated Postgres

observability.name: Observability (OpenLIT + ClickHouse)
observability.purpose:
Stack-wide LLM observability. OpenLIT captures every LLM call that flows
through Open WebUI's pipeline layer (Dify, GPUStack, hermes, moltis,
opencode) and indexes it in ClickHouse for cost / latency / token /
prompt-quality dashboards, with 30-day auto-pruned retention.
user_facing_capabilities: See cost, latency, token usage and prompt/response quality per model and per app.
Drill into individual LLM traces to debug slow or expensive prompts.
use_cases: Track LLM spend and performance trends over time.
Find and fix prompts that blow the token budget or run slow.

talks_to.purpose: receives OTLP traces from the Open WebUI global filter

searxng.name: Search (SearXNG)
searxng.purpose:
A privacy-respecting metasearch engine that aggregates results from 70+
engines without tracking. Runs internal-only as the web-search backend for
Chat and Dify (URL discovery), not exposed as an end-user UI.
user_facing_capabilities: Web-search grounding inside AI chat and Dify workflows (no external tracking).
use_cases: Give chat answers current, web-grounded context.
Discover source URLs to feed into Crawl4AI / RAG ingestion.

crawl4ai.name: Crawl4AI
crawl4ai.purpose:
A RAG-friendly web crawler. Runs headless Chromium under Playwright,
executes JavaScript, and emits clean Markdown / structured JSON suitable
for direct ingestion into knowledge bases. Where SearXNG finds URLs,
Crawl4AI fetches and distils the actual page content.
user_facing_capabilities: Crawl a URL and get clean Markdown/JSON (not just a link).
Use a playground UI to test extraction recipes; call /crawl /scrape /llm via REST.
Feed distilled pages into LightRAG / Cognee / Onyx / Dify knowledge bases.
use_cases: Scheduled ingestion of curated URLs into a knowledge base.
"Read this URL and summarise" on demand from chat.

talks_to.purpose: RAG ingestion + on-demand page distillation via :11235

stts.name: Speech (STT + TTS)
stts.purpose:
Voice services for the stack: speech-to-text via Speaches (OpenAI Whisper)
and text-to-speech via Microsoft Edge TTS. Both are internal APIs consumed
by Open WebUI for voice input and spoken responses.
user_facing_capabilities: Dictate prompts by voice in chat (Whisper transcription).
Have AI responses read aloud (TTS).
Transcribe uploaded audio.
use_cases: Hands-free / accessible AI chat.
Audio note transcription.

gotenberg.name: Document Conversion (Gotenberg)
gotenberg.purpose:
A stateless API that converts HTML, Markdown and Office documents
(DOCX/XLSX/PPTX) to PDF using Chromium + LibreOffice. Used as a backend
for Paperless-ngx and available to Dify document workflows.
user_facing_capabilities: Convert Office and HTML documents to PDF programmatically.
use_cases: Office-to-PDF for archival in Paperless-ngx.
Render report templates to PDF in a workflow.

tika.name: Apache Tika
tika.purpose:
Detects and extracts text, metadata and language from 1000+ file formats
via a simple REST API. Backs Paperless-ngx text extraction and is callable
from Dify document flows.
user_facing_capabilities: Extract text + metadata from heterogeneous files (PDF, Office, email, images, archives).
Detect document language.
use_cases: High-quality text extraction for Paperless-ngx search.
Metadata harvesting in document pipelines.

docling.name: Docling
docling.purpose:
Converts PDF, DOCX, PPTX, images and HTML into structured Markdown/JSON
with layout analysis that preserves tables, headings and reading order.
Exposes a REST API and a Gradio UI; can optionally use a GPUStack
granite-docling vision model for complex layouts. Uses an RQ (valkey)
job engine so the UI works under concurrent load.
user_facing_capabilities: Convert PDFs/scans/Office docs to clean structured Markdown or JSON.
Interactive conversion via a Gradio web UI, or batch via REST.
Optionally apply a vision-language model for hard layouts.
use_cases: PDF → Markdown for RAG ingestion.
Structured extraction from scanned documents (e.g. the PSA CMT demo).

talks_to.purpose: RQ job queue for async conversions

presidio.name: Presidio (PII Detection & Redaction)
presidio.purpose:
Local PII detection, anonymisation and image redaction. The Analyzer finds
30+ PII entity types in text, the Anonymizer masks/replaces them, and the
Image Redactor blacks out PII regions in images — all on-box, no data
leaves the server.
user_facing_capabilities: Detect PII (names, emails, IBANs, card numbers, SSNs, …) in text.
Mask / replace PII before sharing or sending to an LLM.
Black out sensitive regions in images.
use_cases: GDPR-style redaction of documents before sharing.
PII scrubbing in AI pipelines (e.g. the PSA PII-shield flow).

stirling-pdf.name: Stirling-PDF
stirling-pdf.purpose:
A self-hosted web UI for 50+ PDF operations — merge, split, rotate, OCR,
compress, convert, watermark, fill forms, sign, redact — all processed
server-side with nothing leaving the box.
user_facing_capabilities: Merge / split / rotate / reorder PDFs in the browser.
OCR scanned PDFs; compress for email; convert to/from images and Office.
Watermark, sign, fill forms, and redact.
use_cases: Combine invoices; split a large scan; shrink a file to email.
OCR a stack of scanned pages into searchable PDFs.

paperless-ngx.name: Paperless-ngx
paperless-ngx.purpose:
A document management system that scans, OCRs, archives and full-text
indexes paper documents into a searchable web archive, with tag-based
automated filing. Uses Gotenberg for Office→PDF and Tika for extraction.
user_facing_capabilities: Ingest scans/emails, OCR them, and auto-file by tags/correspondents.
Full-text search across the whole document archive.
Browse and download original + archived versions.
use_cases: Paperless office: invoices, receipts, contracts.
Searchable long-term archive of business paperwork.

gitea.name: Git (Gitea)
gitea.purpose:
A lightweight self-hosted Git service with web UI, issue tracking, pull
requests and CI/CD (Gitea Actions). Shares the main Postgres + Valkey.
Git over SSH is available on port 2222.
user_facing_capabilities: Host private Git repositories with a full web UI.
Issues, pull requests, code review, releases, and Actions CI/CD.
Clone/push over HTTPS or SSH (:2222).
use_cases: Private team source control + code review.
Repo backend for OpenHands / Coding-Tools agents and Onyx code indexing.

lightrag.name: LightRAG
lightrag.purpose:
A graph-based RAG knowledge base. Decomposes documents into entities and
relationships and combines entity-level + relationship-level graphs for
more accurate retrieval than flat vector search. Uses GPUStack for
embeddings and LLM-powered graph construction.
user_facing_capabilities: Build a knowledge graph from a document collection and query it.
Dual-level (entity + relationship) retrieval for grounded answers.
use_cases: Q&A over large document corpora with structured retrieval.
Research/literature exploration that follows relationships.

talks_to.purpose: embeddings + LLM extraction (qwen3.6, thinking disabled via chat_template_kwargs)

cognee.name: Cognee (GraphRAG / AI Memory)
cognee.purpose:
A GraphRAG knowledge engine that builds structured knowledge graphs
("brains") from unstructured data and serves as a persistent memory layer
for AI agents. Entity extraction + relationship mapping enable multi-hop
queries across documents and conversations. Exposes an MCP server so
agents (moltis, opencode) can remember/recall over the graph.
user_facing_capabilities: Ingest data into named 'brains' and build queryable knowledge graphs (cognify).
Multi-hop semantic search + graph visualisation in the web UI.
Give agents long-term memory via the cognee MCP tools (remember/recall/search).
use_cases: Persistent memory for moltis / opencode coding agents.
Connect facts across many documents for richer answers.

talks_to.purpose: LLM extraction (openai/qwen3.6, thinking disabled via chat_template_kwargs) + embeddings
metadata (cognee_db); Kuzu graph is embedded on-volume

onyx.name: Onyx (Enterprise Search)
onyx.purpose:
An AI enterprise-search platform that connects to many data sources (Gitea
repos, Paperless documents, web pages) and answers questions semantically
with LLM-generated answers over its own Vespa index + embedding model
servers. One of the heaviest modules (~5 GB RAM).
user_facing_capabilities: Unified semantic search across code and documents with cited LLM answers.
Connectors that index team resources on a schedule.
use_cases: Ask one question and get an answer drawn from code + docs together.
Org-wide knowledge search over connected sources.

matrix.name: Matrix (Synapse + Element)
user_facing_capabilities: Encrypted team chat: rooms, DMs, threads — in the browser via Element.
Single sign-on with stack credentials (OIDC).
Bot/bridge integration (e.g. via the Moltis agent gateway).
use_cases: Internal secure messaging.
Bridge conversations to Telegram/Discord/Slack via Moltis.

vaultwarden.name: Vaultwarden (Password Manager)
vaultwarden.purpose:
A lightweight, Rust-based Bitwarden-compatible password manager. Works with
official Bitwarden browser extensions, desktop and mobile apps; Authentik
OIDC SSO lets users sign in with stack credentials.
user_facing_capabilities: Store and share passwords/secrets in personal and org vaults.
Browser auto-fill via Bitwarden extensions; mobile/desktop apps.
use_cases: Team password management and secure credential sharing.
Developer API-key storage.

infisical.name: Infisical (Secrets Management)
infisical.purpose:
A developer-focused secrets-management platform: store API keys, DB
credentials and config with project + environment scoping (dev/staging/
prod), via web dashboard, CLI and REST API. AI coding agents can pull
secrets at runtime.
user_facing_capabilities: Centralised, environment-scoped secret storage with a web UI + CLI + API.
Runtime secret injection for apps and AI agents (e.g. OpenHands).
use_cases: Single source of secrets for a dev team.
Give an autonomous agent scoped credentials at task time.

agents.name: Personal Agent Manager
agents.purpose:
The orchestrator for per-user AI agents. Authenticated users launch their
own isolated agent containers (Hermes, Moltis, Coding Agents, OpenHands,
Paperclip) with quota-based resource governance, each on its own subdomain,
with dynamic Caddy routing, idle auto-shutdown and stale-instance cleanup.
Admins configure available agent types and quota tiers (Basic/Power/Admin)
in the Config UI.
user_facing_capabilities: Self-provision a personal AI agent from the 'My Agents' drawer.
Each agent runs isolated, per-user, with its own URL + persistent volumes.
Idle agents auto-stop; quota tiers cap resource use per user.
use_cases: Multi-user AI agent platform with per-person isolation.
Give every developer a personal coding agent + memory.

openhands.name: OpenHands (Autonomous Coding Agent)
openhands.purpose:
An autonomous AI software-development agent that writes, runs, tests and
debugs code, spawning per-task sandbox containers. Uses GPUStack for
inference, Gitea for repos/PRs, and Infisical for secrets. Available as a
shared profile and as a per-user agent.
user_facing_capabilities: Give a goal in natural language; the agent writes and runs the code to achieve it.
Create branches/PRs in Gitea; iterate with tests.
use_cases: Automated bug-fixing, feature prototyping, test writing, code review help.

paperclip.name: Paperclip (AI Company Orchestration)
paperclip.purpose:
An experimental "AI company" orchestration platform: hire AI agents, give
them roles and goals, and let them collaborate on automated workflows.
Early-stage and evolving.
user_facing_capabilities: Define agents with roles/goals and have them coordinate on tasks.
Kanban-style tracking of multi-agent work.
use_cases: Experiment with autonomous multi-agent task automation.

hermes.name: Hermes (Personal)
hermes.purpose:
A self-improving Python AI agent (NousResearch) with a workspace UI —
memory browser, skills explorer, terminal, and multi-session support.
Provisioned per user as an isolated personal assistant.
user_facing_capabilities: A personal agent that learns/extends its own Python skills over time.
Browse its memory, explore/edit skills, drive it from a web terminal.
use_cases: A long-lived personal assistant that accumulates skills and context.

moltis.name: Moltis
moltis.purpose:
A Rust personal-agent server with a Matrix, Telegram and Discord gateway,
so a user's agent is reachable from chat platforms. Integrates with the
cognee MCP for long-term memory.
user_facing_capabilities: Talk to your personal agent from Matrix/Telegram/Discord.
Persistent memory via cognee MCP (remember/recall).
use_cases: A chat-platform-native personal assistant/bot.

coding-agent-web.name: Coding Agents
coding-agent-web.purpose:
A persistent per-user coding workspace: an in-browser tmux terminal with a
durable /workspace + /home volume, pre-wired (via a local-model shim) to run
a coding-agent CLI against the local GPUStack LLM. Split (#36 / PR #84) into
per-type images — opencode (opencode-ai CLI), codex (@openai/codex), and a
bare "user-defined" agent that lets a user bring + persist their own CLI
(e.g. `npm i -g @opengsd/gsd-pi`, the retired gsd agent). All four build from
the shared Dockerfile; razzfazz.ai ships only the Apache-2.0 web-terminal
wiring, and every bundled CLI keeps its own upstream licence.
user_facing_capabilities: AI-assisted coding in a browser terminal (opencode / codex / your own CLI).
Persistent per-user workspace; bring-your-own agent survives restarts.
use_cases: Personal AI pair-programmer with a durable workspace.

talks_to.purpose: LLM inference (coding model, via local shim)
